tests.procedure: Under strong white light check each received container separately in a clean transparent watch glass or glass dish for foreign particles, colour and conformity with the visual specification.

details.usp_stm_text: White to practically white crystals or crystalline powder. Is stable in air, and is slowly affected by sunlight. Its solutions have a pH of about 3. (spec sheet gives only the first sentence)
details.bp_stm_text: White or almost white, crystalline powder.

tests.procedure: Weigh 100 mg powdered sample in a stoppered tube; add 0.1 mL solvent, shake vigorously 1 min, hold at 25.0 ± 0.5 °C for 15 min, repeat shake/hold once if not dissolved; stepwise add 0.9 mL, 2 mL, 7 mL solvent (same shake and hold) to classify very soluble / freely soluble / soluble / sparingly soluble; if still undissolved use 10 mg in 10 mL (slightly soluble) then 1 mg in 10 mL (very slightly soluble), else practically insoluble. Repeat with the other solvents.
Measure the melting point with a calibrated melting point apparatus.

details.note: heating rate / capillary details not stated

tests.procedure: UV identification (BP): solution A = 1.0 mL solution S to 50.0 mL with 10.3 g/L HCl; solution B = 1.0 mL A to 100.0 mL with 10.3 g/L HCl; solution C = 1.0 mL A to 100.0 mL with KH2PO4 0.025 M + Na2HPO4 0.025 M solution. Scan B 250-350 nm, C 220-350 nm; read specific absorbances at the maxima.

details.solutionS: 2.50 g in CO2-free water to 50.0 mL
details.solutionA: 1.0 mL S to 50.0 mL with 10.3 g/L hydrochloric acid
details.solutionB: 1.0 mL A to 100.0 mL with 10.3 g/L hydrochloric acid
details.solutionC: 1.0 mL A to 100.0 mL with phosphate solution
details.phosphateSolution: 3.39 g KH2PO4 + 3.53 g Na2HPO4, both dried 2 h at 120 ± 2 °C, in CO2-free water to 1000.0 mL (STM line 42)

tests.procedure: IR identification: mix sample intimately with potassium bromide, compress to a transparent pellet, compare the spectrum with that of Pyridoxine Hydrochloride RS or WS.

USP chloride identification: to a solution containing about 2 mg chloride ion in 2 mL add 1 drop diluted nitric acid and 0.5 mL silver nitrate TS; white curdy precipitate; centrifuge at once, decant, wash precipitate with three 1-mL portions of nitric acid solution (1 in 100), discard washings; add ammonia TS dropwise; it dissolves readily.

details.silverNitrateTS: 0.1 N silver nitrate: about 17.5 g in 1000 mL water
details.ammoniaTS: 350 mL ammonia water diluted to 1000 mL
details.nitricAcidDilute: 20 g nitric acid to 100 mL with water

tests.procedure: TLC identification: test solution 1.0 g in water to 10 mL, then 1 mL to 10 mL; reference solution 0.10 g Pyridoxine Hydrochloride RS or WS in water to 10 mL; TLC silica gel G plate; mobile phase concentrated ammonia : methylene chloride : tetrahydrofuran : acetone 9:13:13:65; apply 2 µL; unsaturated tank, 15 cm path; dry in air; spray 50 g/L sodium carbonate in ethanol (96 per cent) 30 : water 70, dry in air current, spray 1 g/L dichloroquinonechlorimide in ethanol (96 per cent), examine immediately.

BP reaction of chlorides: to 2 mL solution S acidify with dilute nitric acid and add 0.4 mL silver nitrate solution R1; shake, stand; curdled white precipitate; centrifuge, wash with three 1-mL portions of water (rapidly, subdued light); suspend precipitate in 2 mL water, add 1.5 mL ammonia.

details.silverNitrateR1: 4.25 g silver nitrate to 100 mL water
details.solutionS: 2.50 g in CO2-free water to 50.0 mL

tests.procedure: Appearance of solution (BP, Method II): solution S (2.50 g in CO2-free water to 50.0 mL) is compared with reference solution Y7.

details.solutionS: 2.50 g in CO2-free water to 50.0 mL
details.Y7: 2.5 mL standard solution Y (yellow) made up to 100 mL (97.5 mL) with hydrochloric acid (10 g/L)
details.standardSolutionY: yellow solution 2.4 + red solution 0.6 + 7.0 mL hydrochloric acid (10 g/L)
details.yellowSolution: 46 g ferric chloride in about 900 mL of (25 mL HCl + 975 mL water), to 1000.0 mL with the same mixture
details.redSolution: 60 g cobalt chloride in about 900 mL of (25 mL HCl + 975 mL water), to 1000.0 mL with the same mixture

tests.procedure: Weigh empty weighing bottle (previously dried at 105 °C, cooled in desiccator) W1; weigh accurately 1.000 g sample W2; dry (BP: calibrated oven at 105 °C; USP: in vacuum over silica gel for 4 h), cool in desiccator, weigh W3; repeat to constant weight. % LOD = ((W1 + W2) - W3) / W2 x 100.

details.bpDrying: oven 105 °C (time not stated, to constant weight)

tests.procedure: Weigh empty crucible (ignited at 600 ± 50 °C ~30 min, cooled in desiccator) W1; weigh 1.0 g sample W2; moisten with ~1 mL sulfuric acid, char gently on hot plate, moisten residue again with sulfuric acid, heat until white fumes cease, ignite in muffle at 600 ± 50 °C until completely incinerated, cool in desiccator, weigh W3; repeat to constant weight (repeat moistening/ignition in 30 min periods until two weighings differ by no more than 0.5 mg or limit met). % = (W3 - W1) / W2 x 100.

details.constantWeightCriterion: 2 consecutive weighings not differing by more than 0.5 mg
details.note: BP name Sulfated Ash, USP name Residue on Ignition, same procedure and limit

tests.procedure: Content of chloride (USP), titrimetric direct titration: dissolve 500 mg sample in 50 mL methanol, add 5 mL glacial acetic acid and 2-3 drops eosin Y TS; titrate with 0.1 N silver nitrate VS (visual endpoint); blank = 50 mL methanol. Result % = ((VS - VB) x N x F / W) x 100, F = 35.45 mg/mEq, W in mg.

details.additions: 5 mL glacial acetic acid; 2-3 drops eosin Y TS
details.indicator: Eosin Y TS (50 mg in 10 mL water)
details.titrantPreparation: about 17.5 g silver nitrate in 1000 mL water
details.equivalenceFactor: 35.45 mg Cl per mEq (each mL of 1 N titrant = 35.45 mg Cl)
details.formula: Result = [((VS-VB) x N x F)/W] x 100

tests.procedure: Assay (BP, potentiometry): dissolve previously dried 0.150 g in 5 mL anhydrous formic acid, add 50 mL acetic anhydride, titrate with 0.1 M perchloric acid, endpoint potentiometric; blank titration. Each mL of 0.1 M perchloric acid is equivalent to 20.56 mg C8H12ClNO3. Assay % = (E.P x Eq.wt x F / Wt) x 100.

details.solvent: 5 mL anhydrous formic acid + 50 mL acetic anhydride
details.equivalenceFactor: each mL of 0.1 M perchloric acid is equivalent to 20.56 mg of C8H12ClNO3
details.formula: Assay % = (E.P x Eq.wt x F / Wt) x 100; E.P = end point volume, Eq.wt = 20.56 mg, F = titrant factor, Wt = sample weight
details.titrantPreparation: 0.1M Perchloric Acid VS: 8.5 mL perchloric acid in about 900 mL glacial acetic acid, add 30 mL acetic anhydride, to 1000.0 mL with glacial acetic acid, stand 24 h
details.titrantStandardization: 0.170 g potassium hydrogen phthalate in 50 mL anhydrous acetic acid (warm gently if needed), cool protected from air, titrate with the perchloric acid solution, endpoint potentiometric or 0.05 mL crystal violet solution; 1 mL 0.1 M perchloric acid = 20.42 mg C8H5KO4
details.crystalVioletSolution: 0.5 g crystal violet in anhydrous acetic acid to 100 mL

tests.procedure: Assay (USP, HPLC with internal standard). Mobile phase: 10 mL glacial acetic acid + 0.6 g sodium 1-hexanesulfonate + 700 mL water in 1000-mL flask, adjust to pH 3.0 with glacial acetic acid or 1 N NaOH, add 235 mL methanol, dilute to volume with water. Internal standard solution 5 mg/mL p-hydroxybenzoic acid in mobile phase. Standard: 0.5 mg/mL Pyridoxine HCl RS or WS in mobile phase; 10.0 mL + 1.0 mL internal standard solution to 100 mL with mobile phase. Sample: same with sample. Result % = (RU/RS) x (CS/CU) x 100.

details.mobilePhase: 10 mL glacial acetic acid, 0.6 g sodium 1-hexanesulfonate, 700 mL water in 1000 mL flask; pH 3.0 (glacial acetic acid or 1 N NaOH); add 235 mL methanol; dilute with water to volume
details.internalStandard: p-hydroxybenzoic acid, 5 mg/mL in mobile phase
details.standardSolution: 0.5 mg/mL Pyridoxine Hydrochloride RS or WS in mobile phase; 10.0 mL + 1.0 mL internal standard solution diluted to 100 mL with mobile phase
details.sampleSolution: 0.5 mg/mL Pyridoxine Hydrochloride in mobile phase; 10.0 mL + 1.0 mL internal standard solution diluted to 100 mL with mobile phase

systemSuitability.resolution: NLT 2.5 between pyridoxine and p-hydroxybenzoic acid
systemSuitability.rsdRatio: NMT 3.0% for ratios of pyridoxine peak area to internal standard peak area

details.formula: Result = (RU/RS) x (CS/CU) x 100; RU, RS = peak response ratio pyridoxine/internal standard in sample, standard; CS = conc of USP Pyridoxine Hydrochloride RS (mg/mL); CU = conc of sample (mg/mL)

tests.procedure: Related substances (BP, LC): test solution 25 mg in water to 10.0 mL; reference (a) 1.0 mL test solution to 100.0 mL with water then 1.0 mL to 10.0 mL; reference (b) 2.5 mg pyridoxine impurity A RS + 2.5 mg 4-deoxypyridoxine HCl (impurity B) in water to 10.0 mL, then 2.0 mL to 10.0 mL. Column 0.25 m x 4.6 mm base-deactivated end-capped octadecylsilyl silica 5 µm; mobile phase 2.72 g KH2PO4 in 900 mL water, pH 3.0 with dilute phosphoric acid, to 1000 mL; 1.0 mL/min; 210 nm; 5 µL; run time 2.5 x retention of pyridoxine.

details.referenceA: 1.0 mL test solution to 100.0 mL with water; 1.0 mL of this to 10.0 mL with water
details.referenceB: 2.5 mg pyridoxine impurity A RS + 2.5 mg 4-deoxypyridoxine hydrochloride (impurity B) in water to 10.0 mL; 2.0 mL to 10.0 mL with water
details.column: l = 0.25 m, 4.6 mm id; base-deactivated end-capped octadecylsilyl silica gel for chromatography R (5 µm)
details.mobilePhase: 2.72 g KH2PO4 in 900 mL water, adjust to pH 3.0 with dilute phosphoric acid, dilute to 1000 mL with water
details.runTime: 2.5 times the retention time of pyridoxine
details.retention: pyridoxine about 12 min; impurity A about 1.7 relative; impurity B about 1.9 relative
details.systemSuitability: resolution minimum 1.5 between impurity A and impurity B peaks in reference solution (b)
details.quantitation: for each impurity use the concentration of pyridoxine hydrochloride in reference solution (a)

limits.disregardLimit: max 0.05 per cent (STM only, not on spec sheet)

openQuestions.question: Issue request file 'Pyridoxine Hydrochloride__Issue Request Sodium Methyl Paraben.txt' is in fact the issue request for the Pyridoxine Hydrochloride STM (document name, old code C1I-91-242, v1/1), not Sodium Methyl Paraben; it holds no minimum sample quantity, so minQuantity comes from the spec sheets and STM.
openQuestions.source: Pyridoxine Hydrochloride__Issue Request Sodium Methyl Paraben.txt:10-11

openQuestions.question: Minimum quantity: testing = 100 g (spec sheets, STM) and retention = 80 g (STM); no periodic-retest quantity is stated anywhere, so minQuantity.retest is null.

BP assay: a blank titration is required but the formula (E.P x Eq.wt x F / Wt) does not subtract it, and Eq.wt is in mg while the unit of Wt is not stated (g vs mg). Row loaded as is; confirm formula (blank-corrected volume, unit of Wt).

USP Content of Chloride and USP HPLC Assay are specified 'on the dried basis' but the formulas give no loss-on-drying correction (the BP assay uses a previously dried sample). Confirm whether the sample is dried first or the result corrected for LOD.
openQuestions.source: Pyridoxine Hydrochloride__STM-Pyridoxine (004) after edit.txt:53; Pyridoxine Hydrochloride__STM-Pyridoxine (004) after edit.txt:54

openQuestions.question: 0.1 N silver nitrate titrant: only its preparation (about 17.5 g in 1000 mL) is given, no standardization procedure, but the formula needs the actual normality N.
USP HPLC assay: number of replicate injections for the RSD NMT 3.0% requirement and column temperature are not stated.
BP related substances: STM adds a disregard limit of 0.05 per cent that is not on the BP spec sheet (kept in test details only, no row).
Reference solution Y7 recipe: 'Standard solution Y (yellow): Mix 2.4 of yellow solution, 0.6 of red solution and 7.0 ml...' units for 2.4 and 0.6 are missing (mL assumed).
